chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: What is MMTLS?

chat.author: Jim Taft
chat.text: Tencent's custom encryption "based on TLS 1.3"

chat.author: Luigi Iannone
chat.text: My Modified TLS? ;-)

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Someone hasn't discovered Oblivious HTTP it seems.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text:
Jim Taft said:

Tencent's custom encryption "based on TLS 1.3"

Is it specified somewhere?

chat.author: Antoine Fressancourt
chat.text: Telegram is also notorious for their custom encryption algorithms

chat.author: Jim Taft
chat.text: She said there was only one reference to it.  So no.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: I thought she said that it had a reference to TLS 1.3 specs (RFC9846).

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: https://docs.mitmproxy.org/stable/concepts/options/#emudhra

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: So MMTLS is secure?

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: That was never claimed.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: I will point out that Signal rolls its own crypto.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text:
Martin Thomson said:

That was never claimed.

So the only one out of 9 was MMTLS, no?

chat.author: Jonathan Lennox
chat.text: MMTLS wasn't breakable by her in the time she gave to it.  This isn't the same thing as secure.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: Maybe I misunderstood.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Yes, MMTLS + 8 broken protocols, of those analysed.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text:
Jonathan Lennox said:

MMTLS wasn't breakable by her in the time she gave to it.  This isn't the same thing as secure.

That clarifies things for me, thanks.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: I have no confidence that fixing transport security will fix those apps.  Many apps are simply not well built.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: There is a very simple explanation: Hanlon's Razor.

chat.author: Antoine Fressancourt
chat.text: I would rephrase "Security researchers should be hired and paid for ...."

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: If MMTLS is based on TLS 1.3, there's a reasonable chance that it is okay.  No guarantee, because TLS 1.3 has some subtle design aspects that could be easy to unwind, but it is possible even to improve on TLS 1.3.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: https://citizenlab.ca/research/should-we-chat-too-security-analysis-of-wechats-mmtls-encryption-protocol/

chat.text: Maybe a dumb q, not my area of expertise... might there be reluctance to use some standard crypto for fear of source country where algo(s) or libs originated?

chat.author: Junxiao Shi
chat.text: I still remember IE6 showing "certificate revocation information cannot be retrieved" alert box, for almost every website.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: One of the advisors of the speaker invented CRLite, so he well knows that all this talk about OCSP is moot.  Firefox is one of the few browsers that makes OCSP requests (and not for long if our plans pan out).  We are using CRLite now and it is far, far better.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text:
Junxiao Shi said:

I still remember IE6 showing "certificate revocation information cannot be retrieved" alert box, for almost every website.

Zoom still generates a popup any time it can't validate its own server certificate.  Such a terrible piece of software UX.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: https://github.com/mozilla/clubcard/

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Whoops, someone said DNSSEC.  I'm done.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text:
Martin Thomson said:

One of the advisors of the speaker invented CRLite, so he well knows that all this talk about OCSP is moot.  Firefox is one of the few browsers that makes OCSP requests (and not for long if our plans pan out).  We are using CRLite now and it is far, far better.

Is the main idea of CRLite that the client retrieves all CRLs and compare locally? What if CRLs are updated?

chat.author: Dave Plonka
chat.text: Re: Martin's comment, thanks for pointing out the CRLite connect.  It is (still) reasonable for the author to present the [c. 2025] work as awarded the prize and the measurements there. While they may be able to update their result, IRTF wants to highlight the disciplined measurement work even at a past point in time, so we know where we came from and share good measurement examples.

chat.author: David Schinazi
chat.text: If you have a problem and your solution is DNSSEC, congratulations! Now you have two problems

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: Agree with Dave. I will add that being accepted in 2025 means they would have done it maybe a year or so before. Publishing takes time!

chat.author: Dirk Kutscher
chat.text: Yes, the selection took place one year ago.

chat.author: Lixia Zhang
chat.text: a clarification question: certs are revoked in real time, that requires real time signing for new NSEC RRs, right?

chat.author: Karl Dyson
chat.text: Yes, but that happens very quickly if the CA were to dynamically update the applicable zone

chat.author: Shivan Sahib
chat.text: Chromium still honors stapled OCSP. but mostly uses CRLSets

chat.author: Lixia Zhang
chat.text: real-time signing was a no-no back in the early days of DNSSEC development.

chat.author: Dave Plonka
chat.text: Perhaps stating the obvious... we can not make an applied research award unless time passes. Anyway, I didn't take the comment as a criticism, it's a fair observation and opp'y to explain why it is this way. Peace.

chat.author: Karl Dyson
chat.text: For context, we make dynamic updates to zones, the relevant signing activity happens, and the change is in the internet facing zone in <5 seconds typically.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text:
Shivan Sahib said:

Chromium still honors stapled OCSP. but mostly uses CRLSets

CRLSets is the same as CRL retrieval?

chat.author: Karl Dyson
chat.text:
Lixia Zhang said:

real-time signing was a no-no back in the early days of DNSSEC development.

Ah, I'd suggest this isn't live signing on the edge, this is just (!) updates to the zone on the primary server centrally.

chat.author: Shivan Sahib
chat.text: no CRLSets are pushed to clients. if you go to chrome://components (or on Brave, brave://components)  you can see the latest version

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: Why bother with CRLs when short-lived TTLs can give the same result with fewer moving parts?

chat.author: Karl Dyson
chat.text: I think the gradual reduction in certificate validity windows probably overtakes this though @Jim Reid ?

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: Maybe. DNS TTLs can be as low as 1 second. As you know Karl.

chat.author: Karl Dyson
chat.text: I had hear this :D

chat.author: Karl Dyson
chat.text: Yes, aggressive NSEC will give you the window/gap and aid caching, but you'd need, as you say, low TTLs for NSEC and SOA minimum to have new revocations take effect rapidly, I think

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: True. Though doing 1 DNS lookup to get a short-lived cert is a whole lot easier than feeding that cert to a bunch of CRLs to check its validity. YMMV.

chat.author: Lixia Zhang
chat.text: yes, the performance gain comes from structured naming in verification.

chat.author: Karl Dyson
chat.text: Propagation of a newly added revocation record including signing activity etc is achievable in a handful of seconds.

chat.author: Lixia Zhang
chat.text: the early day concern about real time signing came from the need of keeping private key online

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: meetecho, move the camera to speaker please.

chat.author: Karl Dyson
chat.text: Yeah, the private key for signing is online in this scenario, but buried away in the provisioning stack and nowhere near the edge DNS facing the internet.

chat.author: David Schinazi
chat.text: I was going to say "preaching to the choir" but apparently some parts of the IETF have forgotten about the e2e principle

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: Clarification question: what do you mean by e2e principle?

chat.author: Lixia Zhang
chat.text: E2E is fundamental in heterogeneous systems. Mark is talking a completely closed system.

chat.text: https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc3439/#section-2.1

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: Thanks Antoine.

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: Anyone else here remember the time when the Internet core was dumb and the edge devices were smart?:grinning:

chat.author: Lixia Zhang
chat.text: I do. Next interesting topic to chat is why that changed.

chat.text: If only I had that much copper or fiber between me and the sites I visit.

chat.text: MT just make sure you don't replace copper for fiber on a Friday

chat.text: 75,000 GPUs is small for them :slight_smile:

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: Don't be so jealous .. just admire the class

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Not jealous at all.  Mostly just disappointed.  Every such concentration is indicative of a problem in the larger system.

chat.author: Antoine Fressancourt
chat.text: The interesting thing to discuss is what is sticking when the GPUs are heterogeneous, less numerous and linked with less fiber paths between them, across administrative domains.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: I wonder how much attestation evidence 75,000 GPUs will contain if I were to attest those, and how would I send it within the TLS handshake?

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: It will take time to see Ai training fabrics build to run over WAN

chat.author: Robert Raszuk
chat.text: Inference does but this is completly different

chat.author: Antoine Fressancourt
chat.text: Distributed inference is more of an Internet thing than training (even if federated pretaining projects are interesting)

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: And one needs event logs for those GPUs too. So it is going to be a massive failure of the TLS handshake.

chat.author: Steve Traugott
chat.text: $brain keeps trying to figure out the control plane, then looking at slide where the control plane doesn't even need to be up, then repeat.  I think what I'm missing is how those path lists get shared with senders?

chat.author: Dirk Kutscher
chat.text: sorry, this has to be the last question

chat.text: The trick, I guess, is that the topology is known from the start
